With `rebase.missingCommitsCheck` set to `error`, if a commit is removed from the interactive todo list, Git will print a warning and stop the rebase process. This prevents the rebase from proceeding until the issue is resolved. To correct the todo list, you can use `git rebase --edit-todo` to manually adjust the list and ensure all commits are accounted for before continuing the rebase.

Source 2:  
When `rebase.missingCommitsCheck` is set to "error", git rebase -i will print a warning if some commits are removed (e.g. a line was deleted), however the rebase will still proceed. If set to "error", it will print the previous warning and stop the rebase, 'git rebase --edit-todo' can then be used to correct the error.
